svg.title: Protocol selection matrix by requirement, with the six principles that outrank the matrix
svg.desc: A matrix with requirements as rows and four protocols as columns: OSPF, IS-IS, EIGRP and BGP. Strong fit is marked with a filled dot, workable with an open dot, weak with a dash. Rows: single vendor campus, multivendor requirement, more than 500 routers in one domain, sub-second convergence need, rich policy and path control, segment routing core, and team already trained. OSPF is strong for campus, multivendor and trained teams, workable at scale, weak for policy. IS-IS is strong at scale, for segment routing and multivendor, weak for team familiarity. EIGRP is strong for single vendor campus and convergence, weak for multivendor and policy. BGP is strong for policy and scale, weak for campus simplicity. A right-hand panel lists six principles: use one IGP plus BGP rather than three IGPs; choose by operating model; keep the flooding domain small; design the addressing plan before the protocol; test failure not configuration; and write the decision down with its reason.
svg.text: Choose the protocol by requirement, then let the operating model break the tie
Filled dot = strong fit · open dot = workable · dash = poor fit. The matrix narrows the field; it does not pick the winner
REQUIREMENT
OSPF
IS-IS
EIGRP
BGP
Single-vendor campus
Multivendor requirement
More than 500 routers in one domain
Sub-second convergence with a small team
Rich policy and path control
Segment routing core
Team already trained and on call
SIX PRINCIPLES THAT OUTRANK ANY MATRIX
1. One IGP plus BGP, not three IGPs. Each extra protocol doubles the redistribution surface.
2. Choose by operating model: who is on call, and what they can debug at 3 a.m.
3. Keep the flooding domain small. The protocol will not save a topology that is too flat.
4. Design the addressing plan before the protocol — summarization is a product of the plan.

5. Test failure, not configuration: shut the link, kill the process, pull the power, and measure. 6. Write the decision and its reason in the design document, or the next team will re-decide it by rumour.
